findings.title: join() can leave flusher processes running when timeout expires
findings.body: SpanFlusher.join computes a deadline and, if remaining time is <= 0 before waiting on a process, breaks out of the process-wait loop. This skips `process.terminate()` for the remaining processes. In addition, `deadline = time.time() + timeout if timeout else None` treats a timeout of 0 as no timeout. During shutdown or rebalance with a small timeout, flusher processes may outlive join(), causing leaked processes and possible duplicate flushing/production.

findings.title: Unhealthy flusher worker is replaced without ensuring the old worker stopped
findings.body: _ensure_processes_alive kills a multiprocessing worker (and does nothing for threads created when `produce_to_pipe` is set), then immediately creates a replacement without waiting for the old worker to exit or cleaning up the old process object. If the old worker is still running, it can continue flushing the same shards and shares the same health/backpressure Values with the replacement, which can cause duplicate Kafka production, Redis state races, and leaked process handles.

findings.title: Omitted flusher_processes defaults to one worker per shard, inconsistent with CLI default
findings.body: SpanFlusher treats `max_processes=None` as `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, while the CLI option defaults to 1. Any non-CLI construction of ProcessSpansStrategyFactory or SpanFlusher that omits `flusher_processes` will spawn one process/thread per shard instead of the previous single flusher, which can unexpectedly create many workers and connections. The default should be explicit and consistent, or documented.

findings.title: --flusher-processes accepts invalid non-positive values
findings.body: The new `--flusher-processes` option is declared as plain `type=int` with no lower bound. A negative value reaches SpanFlusher, where `num_processes` becomes negative and `process_to_shards_map` is empty, causing shard assignment to fail. A value of 0 is also silently coerced by `max_processes or len(...)`. Validate the option with something like `click.IntRange(min=1)`.

findings.title: Added sleep in test is ineffective because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: test_basic globally monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op, then calls `time.sleep(0.1)` to give flusher threads time to process. The patched call does not actually wait, so the test is not synchronizing deterministically with the flusher and may become flaky. Use an unpatched sleep or poll for a deterministic condition.
